{{nihongo|'''Mita Hachiman Shrine'''|御田八幡神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Musashi Province]].

Its principal deity is {{ill|Emperor Ōjin|Q317997|qid=Q317997|qid=Q317997|lt=Hondawake-no-Mikoto}} (Hachiman deity), with {{ill|Ame-no-Koyane|Q2564508|qid=Q2564508|lt=Ame-no-Koyane-no-Mikoto}} and {{ill|Takenouchi no Sukune|Q1073668|qid=Q1073668|lt=Takenouchi no Sukune-no-Mikoto}} as associated deities.

It stands on a slope facing the sea side. In the {{ill|Edo period|ar|فترة إيدو|ast|Periodu Edo|az|Edo dövrü|bcl|Panahon nin Edo|be|Перыяд Эда|bg|Едо (период)|bn|এদো যুগ|bo|ཨེ་དོའི་དུས་སྐབས།|br|Marevezh Edo|ca|Període Edo|ckb|سەردەمی ئێدۆ|cs|Období Edo|cv|Эдо тапхăрĕ|da|Edo-perioden|de|Edo-Zeit|eo|Epoko de Edo|es|Período Edo|et|Edo ajastu|eu|Edo aroa|fa|دوره ادو|fi|Edo-kausi|fr|Époque d'Edo|gl|Período Edo|he|תקופת אדו|hi|एदो अवधी|hr|Edo (razdoblje)|hu|Edo-kor|id|Zaman Edo|is|Jedótímabilið|it|Periodo Edo|ja|江戸時代|jv|Jaman Édo|ko|에도 시대|lt|Edo laikotarpis|lv|Edo periods|mk|Едо (период)|mn|Эдогийн эрин|ms|Zaman Edo|nl|Edoperiode|nn|Edotida|oc|Periòde Edo|pl|Edo (okres)|pt|Período Edo|ro|Perioada Edo|ru|Период Эдо|simple|Edo period|sk|Obdobie Edo|sl|Obdobje Edo|sq|Periudha Edo|sr|Едо период|su|Période Edo|sv|Edoperioden|th|ยุคเอโดะ|tl|Panahong Edo|tok|tenpo pi kulupu lawa Eto|tr|Edo Dönemi|uk|Період Едо|ur|ایڈو دور|uz|Edo davri|vi|Thời kỳ Edo|war|Panahon Edo|wuu|江戶時代|zh|江户时代|zh_min_nan|Edo sî-tāi|zh_yue|江戶時代|qid=Q184963}}, the {{ill|Tōkaidō (region)|Q1196306|qid=Q1196306}} ran right in front, and beyond it opened the shore of {{ill|Edo Bay|Q11551101|qid=Q11551101}}, likely giving scenic views. This changed when reclamation of {{ill|Shibaura|Q13489497|qid=Q13489497}} began in the Meiji 40s. Tree pruning around the shrine is kept minimal, leaving a dim and quiet atmosphere. On the rear high ground is adjacent {{ill|Kamezuka Park|Q458122|qid=Q458122}}.

In {{ill|Heisei era|Q234510|qid=Q234510}} 21, to commemorate 1300 years of enshrinement, a regular periodic grand festival was held on August 1 and a mikoshi procession on August 2.

===History===
In {{ill|Wadō (era)|Q1373026|qid=Q1373026}} 2 ({{ill|709|Q23514|qid=Q23514}}), it began as a shrine of protection for the eastern provinces, enshrined at Makioka in Musashi. In {{ill|Kankō|Q2736722|qid=Q2736722}} 7 ({{ill|1011|Q19238|qid=Q19238}}), it was moved to Kubo-Mita, Mita-gō, Musashi, and revered as clan shrine of the Watanabe branch of {{ill|Saga Genji|Q11477318|qid=Q11477318}}. In the '{{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932}}' it is recorded as "Hieda Shrine" in Ebara District, Musashi. (The "Engishiki Hieda Shrine" also has other candidate shrines, including {{ill|Hieta Shrine|Q11596288|qid=Q11596288}} in Kamata, {{ill|Ōta, Tokyo|Q217234|qid=Q217234}}, and {{ill|Rokugō Shrine|Q17215324|qid=Q17215324}} in Higashi-Rokugō.)

When {{ill|Tokugawa Ieyasu|Q171977|qid=Q171977}} entered Edo Castle, an auspicious sign was said to have occurred, and he opened and developed the coast of Kami-Takanawa village (Ebara District) at the current site, building shrine structures there. Relocation was carried out in August {{ill|Kanbun (era)|Q1146228|qid=Q1146228}} 2 ({{ill|1662|Q7574|qid=Q7574}}). However, a great fire in February Kanbun 8 burned all shrine buildings, and a temporary shrine was placed at Yakushi-ji on {{ill|Isarago-zaka|Q11379690|qid=Q11379690}}. Shrine buildings were rebuilt and relocated again in August Kanbun 12.

In {{ill|Keiō|Q776775|qid=Q776775}} 1 ({{ill|1865|Q7708|qid=Q7708}}), the {{ill|Jingi-kan|Q108166762|qid=Q108166762|lt=Jingikan}} renamed it "Hieda Shrine" as in Engishiki; in {{ill|Meiji era|Q3125096|qid=Q3125096}} 5 ({{ill|1874|Q7761|qid=Q7761}}) it was renamed "Mita Hachiman Shrine" and ranked gōsha; in {{ill|1897|Q7847|qid=Q7847}} (Meiji 30) it reverted to '''Mita Hachiman Shrine'''{{sfn|東京都神社庁}}. Shrine buildings from Kanbun 12 were burned in the 1945 Tokyo air raids and rebuilt postwar in {{ill|Shōwa era|Q327567|qid=Q327567}} 29.

===Structures===
* Shrine complex - honden, heiden, haiden
* Precinct shrines - Gokō Inari Shrine, Ontake Shrine
* Precinct land - 2,975.9 m²
* Precinct buildings - kaguraden, temizuya, shamusho
